title: Substituir mecanismo next_id por file-per-issue (scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNN.json)
description: O formato atual (issues.local.json: array + next_id counter) tem tres problemas estruturais. (1) next_id fica stale: qualquer gravacao fora do fluxo normal (hand-filing, commit direto na main, bug do cam issue) dessincroniza o counter do max(id) real — exige reconciliacao manual. Vimos isso no CAM-86/87: next_id=81 enquanto CAM-86 ja existia. (2) Multi-writer collision: dois processos gravando o mesmo arquivo criam conflito de merge no array inteiro, nao so na entrada nova. (3) Branch entanglement: qualquer issue filado numa branch de trabalho toca o mesmo arquivo que a main usa como backlog — merge ou rebase carrega o issue pra branch errada ou conflita. O fix do CAM-86 (commit-tree via index temporario) e um workaround pra isso, nao uma solucao. REDESIGN: um arquivo por issue em scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNN.json (zero-padded 3 digitos). Sem next_id armazenado: o proximo ID e derivado em runtime como max(parseInt(ls scripts/cam/issues/)) + 1. BENEFICIOS: (a) sem counter stale — o max e sempre correto por construcao; (b) branches nunca conflitam no mesmo arquivo — cada issue e um arquivo independente; (c) git blame por issue; (d) hand-filing e criar um arquivo, nao editar um array. MIGRACAO: script que le issues.local.json e escreve um arquivo por issue + deleta issues.local.json. ONDE TOCAR: src/commands/issue.ts (leitura/escrita), src/commands/dashboard.ts (listagem), cam-plan.md (leitura do backlog), scripts/cam/issues.local.json (substituido pelo diretorio), tests. Checar se alguma outra parte do codigo referencia issues.local.json diretamente. Manter o prefixo CAM- e formato de id identico para nao quebrar referencias existentes nos PRDs/handoffs. Prioridade P2: o workaround do CAM-86 resolve o sintoma mais urgente (commit na branch certa), mas enquanto o formato de arquivo unico persistir o problema de counter stale e merge conflict segue latente.

spec.scope: Full robust file-per-issue cutover of the local issue system, NO slicing (operator chose robustness over speed). Replace the monolithic scripts/cam/issues.local.json (array plus next_id counter) with ONE file per issue at scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNNN.json (4-digit zero-padded FILENAME; the id field stays unpadded CAM-NN to preserve PRD/handoff/journal references). Single atomic PR (no dual-format logic): on the branch all code reads/writes the dir; on main until merge it is the array; an operator filing-freeze avoids cross-format filing. Work: (1) generalize the on-main helper (src/git/on-main.ts) to a MULTI-FILE atomic commit (list of {path,content} into one temp index, one write-tree, one commit-tree) with compare-and-swap update-ref (update-ref refs/heads/main <new> <old-expected>) plus a bounded retry loop on concurrent-commit failure, which hardens ALL on-main writers against silent last-writer-wins loss; (2) readBacklogFromMain primitive (git ls-tree -r --name-only main scripts/cam/issues/ plus ONE git cat-file --batch, assembled and numerically sorted by parsed id) preserving the read-from-main cross-branch invariant in O(1) subprocesses; (3) allocateId = max(parsed ids on main) + 1 at write time, with the CAS retry re-reading max on conflict; (4) convert all writers (issue-file, issue-specify, triage, ship-finalize) and all readers (select.ts, dashboard, cam-plan) and index.ts dispatch to the dir via those primitives; (5) idempotent migration that reads the LIVE main issues.local.json, writes N CAM-NNNN.json files, and deletes issues.local.json in ONE atomic multi-file commit, run LATE at finalize after merging origin/main into the branch so any straggler is captured; (6) update scripts/cam/issues.schema.json to the per-file schema, both dual-copies of cam-issue/cam-plan/cam-spec.md and subagent-orchestrator.md, the ADR docs/adr/0001, docs/recovery-runbook.md, scripts/cam/patterns.md, and re-embed src/vendor/_generated.ts; convert the ~10 affected tests. HARD REQUIREMENT: zero vestiges of the old model afterward.
acceptanceCriteria: The on-main helper (src/git/on-main.ts) commits a LIST of {path,content} file-writes in ONE atomic commit-tree (single-file is the 1-element case), used by triage (N rank writes) and the migration (N issue files) [oracle: bun test asserts a multi-file write lands all files in one commit and a mid-list failure writes none]

The on-main update-ref uses compare-and-swap (update-ref refs/heads/main <new> <old-expected>) and a bounded retry loop: a concurrent commit that moved main makes the CAS fail and the writer re-reads and rebuilds rather than silently overwriting [oracle: real-git integration test simulates a concurrent main advance between read and update-ref and asserts no commit is lost]

readBacklogFromMain assembles the backlog from main via git ls-tree plus a single git cat-file --batch (not one git show per file) and sorts numerically by parsed id; the read-from-main cross-branch invariant is preserved [oracle: bun test plus integration: a just-filed issue is visible from another branch; subprocess count is O(1) not O(N)]

allocateId derives the next id as max(parsed ids present on main) + 1 at write time (no stored counter); two concurrent allocations do not collide (the CAS retry re-allocates the loser) [oracle: real-git integration test: two back-to-back allocations against a moving main yield distinct sequential ids]

All writers (issue-file, issue-specify, triage, ship-finalize) and readers (select.ts, dashboard listing, cam-plan backlog read) and the index.ts dispatch operate on scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNNN.json via the new primitives; none reads or writes issues.local.json directly [oracle: bun test per converted module plus the no-vestiges grep in the dedicated criterion]

Issues are stored at scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNNN.json (4-digit zero-padded filename) while the id field stays unpadded CAM-NN; correctness relies on numeric sort, not lexical filename order [oracle: file-assert a migrated issue file is named CAM-0090.json and its id field is CAM-90; bun test sorts >999 correctly]

The migration is idempotent and atomic: it reads the live main issues.local.json, writes one CAM-NNNN.json per issue, and deletes issues.local.json in a single multi-file commit; a second run is a no-op [oracle: real-git integration test migrates a multi-issue array to the dir, asserts issues.local.json gone and every issue present, and re-run produces no new commit]

scripts/cam/issues.schema.json (and its templates copy) describes the per-file issue schema; the old array-plus-next_id schema is gone [oracle: file-assert the schema has no next_id and no top-level issues array, and validates a single CAM-NNNN.json shape]

NO VESTIGES: a repo-wide grep for issues\.local\.json and \bnext_id\b returns ZERO matches across live code (src/), command docs (.claude/commands and templates/commands), agent personas (both copies), schemas, docs/adr and docs/recovery-runbook.md and scripts/cam/patterns.md, README, and src/vendor/_generated.ts, EXCEPT four documented exceptions: append-only history (journal.md, journal.archive.md, lessons.archive.md), issue-content fields (the description/spec text inside CAM-NNNN.json files), the migration module (which must name the old file to read and delete it), and historical CHANGELOG entries [oracle: file-assert grep -rn over the enumerated live surface returns 0 outside the four exceptions]

issues.local.json no longer exists in the repo, is not shipped by cam init (no templates copy), and is not present in the embedded templatesContents map [oracle: file-assert test ! -f scripts/cam/issues.local.json AND no templates path for it AND grep src/vendor/_generated.ts has no issues.local.json template key]
Both dual-copies of every touched doc/schema are updated and the embed is regenerated [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check is green]
Typecheck passes and the full gate spine is green [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: NO slicing: operator chose the full robust cutover over a sliced shortcut. The PRD is large (~9-10 stories); review may exceed the 3-round cap (CAM-78/109 lineage) and that is acceptable, raise the cap for a confirming round rather than abandoning robustness.

FILING FREEZE during the CAM-90 cycle: the orchestrator must NOT file any issue to main (cam issue --file-local writes main issues.local.json in the OLD format) while the branch is migrating away from it; a mid-cycle filing is clobbered by the format-changing delete at squash-merge and is NOT recoverable by the usual merge-origin/main-before-finalize trick (formats diverge). Hold any new issue idea until CAM-90 merges. Re-run the migration at finalize AFTER merging origin/main into the branch to capture any straggler.

Atomic cutover, no dual-format logic: one PR converts all code and runs the migration; on the branch the code is dir-only, on main until merge it is array-only; the filing-freeze (not a runtime if-exists branch) bridges the gap.

The migration module is the ONE justified place that names issues.local.json (it reads and deletes it); it persists as the downstream migration path for cam init projects still on the old format. The no-vestiges oracle excludes it, plus append-only history, issue-content fields, and historical CHANGELOG entries.
id field stays CAM-NN (unpadded); only the FILENAME is 4-digit padded. Padding is cosmetic (clean ls); correctness uses numeric sort. Do not pad the id field or PRD/handoff/journal references break.

The CAS update-ref plus bounded retry hardens ALL on-main writers (issue-file, issue-specify, triage, ship-finalize, journal-append), not just id allocation; today update-ref is a blind overwrite and any concurrent pair can silently lose a commit.

Dual-copy plus embed rule: cam-issue.md, cam-plan.md, cam-spec.md, and subagent-orchestrator.md each have a .claude/ runtime copy and a templates/ copy; issues.schema.json has both copies too. Update both and regenerate src/vendor/_generated.ts (embed-vendor:check is the gate).

CAM-90 obsoletes CAM-121 (harden finalize commit-tree on stale branch copy) and resolves the CAM-113 class (string issueNumber parsed as 0); note/close those when CAM-90 ships. Builds on CAM-106 (state machine, shipped) and the on-main helper from CAM-124 (shipped via CAM-108).
domainTerms: file-per-issue: backlog storage where each issue is scripts/cam/issues/CAM-NNNN.json (4-digit padded filename), replacing the monolithic issues.local.json array plus next_id counter.
allocateId: runtime id allocation = max(parsed ids on main) + 1 at write time, with CAS plus bounded retry, replacing the stored stale-prone next_id counter.

readBacklogFromMain: the read primitive that assembles the backlog from main scripts/cam/issues/ via git ls-tree plus a single git cat-file --batch, numerically sorted by parsed id, preserving the read-from-main cross-branch invariant.
on-main CAS commit: the multi-file atomic commit-tree-to-main with compare-and-swap update-ref (old-expected) plus bounded retry, hardening every on-main writer against silent concurrent-commit loss.

no-vestiges invariant: post-cutover, no live code/doc/schema/template/embed references the old model (issues.local.json or next_id), excluding append-only history, issue-content fields, the migration module, and historical CHANGELOG entries.
filing freeze: the operational rule that no issue is filed to main during the CAM-90 cycle, because a mid-cycle old-format filing would be clobbered by the format-changing cutover at squash-merge.
